Kyro AI builds the software behind that effort: workforce and contractor management for electric utilities, storm restoration contractors, and aggregators. We are headquartered in Plano, Texas, and were spun off from Think Power Solutions, so we pair long-standing utility expertise with the pace and ownership of a product company.<br><br><a href="https://kyro.ai/">https://kyro.ai/</a></p> <p>WHY JOIN KYRO<br>- Work that matters: our platform helps communities get power back after storms and keeps a critical, regulated industry compliant.<br>- A growing product suite: StormShield for storm restoration, Kyro Capital for contractor invoice factoring, KORY (our AI copilot), and contractor onboarding and verification.<br>- Credibility from day one: you sell with the backing of real utility relationships and domain know-how.<br>- Close to leadership: direct access to the CEO and product team, and what you hear from customers shapes the roadmap.<br>- Room to grow: a clear path from SDR to Account Executive.<br>- Flexibility: fully remote team.</p> <p>THE ROLE<br>As an SDR, you are the first conversation most utilities and contractors have with Kyro. You will work two segments with very different buying motions:</p> <p>Utilities (enterprise): You will talk to storm response, emergency management, contractor management, supply chain, and procurement leaders. Cycles are long, involve multiple stakeholders, and are often tied to RFIs/RFPs. A win is a qualified discovery meeting or demo handed to the account team.</p> <p>Contractors (SMB to mid-market): You will talk to owners, operations managers, and storm coordinators at line, vegetation, and restoration contractors. Cycles are shorter, phone-first, and owner-led. A win is a demo held and the contractor signed up and onboarded.</p> <p>WHAT YOU'LL DO<br>- Prospect outbound: research target utilities and contractors, build account lists, and reach decision-makers by phone, email, and LinkedIn.<br>- Own the follow-up: run multi-touch cadences, chase no-shows and stalled conversations, and make sure every lead has a dated next step.<br>- Respond to inbound leads the same business day and qualify them before they go cold.<br>- Qualify with rigor: confirm need, timeline, decision process, budget, and compliance requirements before booking.<br>- Book and confirm demos, send reminders, and hand off with clear notes.<br>- Drive conversions: stay with contractors after the demo until they sign up and start onboarding; keep utility opportunities moving to the next stage.<br>- Keep the CRM clean: log every activity, stage change, and next step.<br>- Feed the product team: share objections, competitor mentions, and feature requests from the field.</p> <p>HOW SUCCESS IS MEASURED<br>Success is measured on demos held and the conversions that follow. Activity counts are leading indicators, not the goal. KPIs: demos booked, demos held, demo-to-opportunity rate, conversions (contractors signed up and onboarded; utility opportunities advanced to proposal or pilot), pipeline sourced, speed to lead, follow-up coverage (share of open leads with a dated next step), and outreach activity. Targets are set separately for each segment; utility credit weighs meetings and pipeline more than closed conversions.</p> <p>WHAT YOU BRING<br>- 1-3 years as an SDR or BDR in B2B sales, ideally SaaS, with a record of hitting or beating meeting and demo quotas<br>- Disciplined follow-up across phone, email, and LinkedIn without being reminded<br>- Confident cold calling, including with field-oriented buyers who rarely live in their inbox<br>- Clear, concise written communication<br>- Hands-on experience with a CRM and a sales engagement tool (HubSpot, Apollo, Outreach, Salesloft, or similar)<br>- Comfort with metrics: you track your own funnel and know where deals stall<br>- Ability to learn a technical, regulated domain quickly<br>- Self-directed and organized in a fully remote setting<br>- Native English speaker, available during US Central Time business hours</p> <p>NICE TO HAVE<br>- Experience selling into utilities, energy, construction, field services, or regulated industries<br>- Familiarity with storm restoration, line work, vegetation management, or contractor ecosystems<br>- Exposure to both enterprise (long-cycle) and SMB or self-serve sales motions<br>- Experience selling workforce management, compliance, or fintech products<br>- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience</p> <p>COMPENSATION AND PROBATION<br>- Competitive market base plus uncapped commission. Base is paid bi-weekly and commission quarterly.<br>- Accelerators: 1.5x at 101-125% of quota, 2.0x above 125%.<br>- The first six months are probationary, with performance reviews at 3 and 6 months against ramped KPI targets (demos held, conversions, follow-up coverage). <br>- If targets are not met, Kyro may extend the probationary period or end employment. - - Employment remains at-will during and after probation.</p> <p>WHAT WE OFFER<br>- Competitive base and variable pay<br>- A fully remote role<br>- A clear path to Account Executive for SDRs who consistently hit target<br>- Direct exposure to product and leadership at a company shaping how utilities run storm response</p> <p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative</a></p> Tue, 13 Oct 2026 17:13:53 +0000 Thu, 12 Nov 2026 17:13:53 +0000 https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/kyro-ai-sales-development-representative Airbnb: Senior Manager, Quality, Volume Tiers Anywhere in the World 🇨🇦 Canada California Management and Finance Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/6567/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> United States <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/">https://careers.airbnb.com/life-at-airbnb/</a> </p> <p>Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost ever

GLM-Legal is a legal AI model from Z.ai, built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained for agentic legal work. It targets contract review, evidence analysis and compliance research. The key result is a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) . That is nearly 3x its base model’s 6.7%. For developers, the catch is access: the API is application-only for now. TL;DR Size: Built on GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-total, 18B-active MoE with a 1M-token context and 128K max output. Z.ai lists no separate GLM-Legal parameter count. Runs on: Z.ai’s hosted API only, by application. No public weights. The base model self-hosts on multi-GPU servers via vLLM or SGLang, with FP8 weights. Performance: Top-10 on Harvey LAB at a fraction of frontier cost. Within 2.3 points of the LegalBench leader. Best: 19.17% Harvey LAB task pass rate, #7 of 79 on Vals AI, at $0.15 per test. Worst: 41.83% on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, below its own base model (45.19%). Bottom line: Best: frontier-class legal agent scores at about 1/128 the cost of Claude Fable 5. Worst: gated beta with no price, no weights and slow runs (1h12m per task). What is GLM-Legal? GLM-Legal is a domain-specialized version of GLM-5.3-Flash for law firms, in-house counsel and compliance teams. The base is Z.ai’s first natively multimodal GLM-5 model . It has 320B total parameters with 18B active. It mixes sparse and linear attention to cut long-context serving cost. It reads text, images, video and files, and outputs text. How was GLM-Legal trained? Training ran in 2 stages: Mid-training on expanded legal corpora, to strengthen reasoning from facts to rules to conclusions. Post-training with reinforcement learning across tens of thousands of legal task environments . The Z.ai team also describes the agent harness co-evolving with the model during post-training. Edge cases in training exposed harness bottlenecks. Harness fixes then exposed the model to more realistic constraints. How does GLM-Legal score on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark? Harvey LAB is an open-source benchmark of 1,250 tasks across 24 practice areas . Over 75,000 expert-written rubric criteria grade the work. A task passes only if every criterion passes. Harvey calls this all-pass grading. Vals AI runs the held-out set with 2 LLM judges and internet disabled . Agents get file tools plus docx , pptx and xlsx skills. On that leaderboard, GLM-Legal scores 19.17% and ranks #7 of 79. Its base, GLM-5.3-Flash, scores 6.67%. The 12.5-point lift is the core claim, and an independent evaluator reproduced it. The post Google Releases Gemini 4 Argon API With 1M Token Output Limit appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Google DeepMind has made Gemini 4 Argon generally available to developers, enterprises and paid Gemini subscribers. Gemini 4 Argon is a sparse mixture-of-experts frontier model from Google built for long, multi-step work. Its target domains are coding, finance, legal, science and cybersecurity. Google first announced Argon on September 30 for a small group of cyber defenders. It now reaches the paid Gemini API at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens. The key change for developers is output length: Argon can write up to 1M tokens in one response. TL;DR Size: Parameter count not disclosed (sparse MoE). 1M token window shared by input and output. Runs on: Google’s cloud only, via Gemini API, AI Studio and Gemini platform. Trained on TPUs. No open weights. Performance: Leads Google’s table on knowledge work, long context and video. Mixed on agentic coding. Best: 91.7% on LVBench (long video understanding). Worst: 55.0% on FrontierSWE v2, last of 4 models in Google’s table. What is Gemini 4 Argon? According to the model card , Argon is a new model, not a fine-tune of an earlier Gemini. It is a large-scale sparse MoE transformer with native multimodal support. It accepts text, images, audio and video, and it outputs text. Google trained it on TPUs using JAX and ML Pathways. The knowledge cutoff is March 2026. Google has not disclosed total or active parameter counts. How does the 1M token output limit work? Google raised the output limit to 1M tokens, up from 64K on earlier Gemini models. The model card describes a combined input plus output window of up to 1M tokens. So a long prompt reduces the room left for output. Google documents a new continuation protocol for long decodes in its developer docs and enterprise docs . At introductory pricing, a full 1M token response costs $10 in output tokens. How does Gemini 4 Argon perform on benchmarks? Google compares Argon with GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5. Argon posts the top score on most rows. DeepSWE v1.1: 77.9%, ahead of Opus 5.5 (74.2%) and GPT-6 Astra (74.1%). Vals Index: 68.90%, ranked #1 by Vals AI ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (67.04%). AutomationBench: 51.3%, versus 42.5% for Opus 5.5. Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark: 19.6%, nearly 3x the next model, but still a low absolute score. GraphWalks, 256K to 1M tokens: 84.2%, versus 71.8% for GPT-6 Astra. CWE-bench v1: 68.0%, tied with GPT-6 Astra. Google also reports 87% on the ERQA embodied reasoning benchmark .
